This is independently flagged by inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics as LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and by reference_inspection_facts.diagnostics as W_DEADLOCK_LEAF (reason=no_outgoing_transition), and verify_facts.checks confirms the deadlock check for this state is refuted with outgoing_count=0. Unlike EmergencyStopping, which has an explicit exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected edge back into InMotion, Stopping has no such continuation.
candidates.reason: The Stopping leaf's total absence of outgoing transitions is a distinct, deterministically certified deadlock-frontier fact (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF, refuted deadlock check) that goes beyond the already-satisfied transition_endpoints contract for InMotion->Stopping; behavior-consequence auditing requires flagging this dead-end continuation gap separately, per protocol distinguishing endpoint existence from deadlock/dead-end consequence.
candidates.requirement_quote: the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: No supplied NL contract explicitly designates Stopping as a formal termination_state with completion semantics; the NL text only requires the transition into Stopping to exist (already satisfied by tr_0008/transition:line:30), and a train arriving and stopping may be an intentionally natural terminal narrative point rather than a violation, since no state_role=termination_state contract governs Stopping and no explicit progress/response obligation is attached to it in the supplied NL closure.
candidates.title: Stopping is a reachable dead-end leaf with no outgoing continuation

cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 explicitly enumerates and counts three named direct substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by the InMotion composite, which is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation rather than a region/partition claim; no explicit parallel/orthogonal region language appears in NL4. The owner is the InMotion composite itself, matching the exact source_id 'InMotion' and the owned ModelIR state ref for InMotion (state:InMotion:line:10).

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root/owner entry, cross-wrapper reachability, event-consumer operational coverage, stable termination, and dead-end frontiers. Key findings: (1) InMotion has a top-level self-loop back to InMotion via the exit_Send route (guard R45RouteToken==7), which is a satisfied endpoint, not a defect. (2) InMotion->Stopping (tr transition:line:30) exists and is exact, but Stopping is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF), which is a genuine dead-end/deadlock-frontier defect since Stopping is reached via the Arrived-signal alternative described by NL2 as one of two required continuation branches for a train-motion system that should be able to resume/complete gracefully; however, no explicit progress/termination contract makes Stopping an intended completion state, so I raise this via a derived deadlock_freedom obligation on the InMotion->Stopping alternative scope using V1. (3) EmergencyStopping is not a stable sink: it has an outgoing edge (exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected) back into InMotion, and its declared event_consumer for exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected is reachable, so it is NOT a violation - EmergencyStopping properly cycles back into operating behavior (satisfied, omitted). (4) The Approaching->[*] retention/exit and event-consumer facts for Approached_Decelerate, Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, and Obstacle_Detected are all reachable and consumed within InMotion's substates, satisfying NL3-CONSUMER-1's event_consumer_coverage obligation (declared_ref and reachable_consumer_state_refs both include Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching, and top-level InMotion->EmergencyStopping (transition:line:31) is reachable) so NL3-CONSUMER-1 is satisfied and omitted. (5) NL10 state_retention for Approaching: the FCSTM shows Approaching has three outgoing edges (to [*] via exit_Send/Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived/Obstacle_Detected) all gated by real trigger events, so retention until the ready condition is structurally represented via triggers, not a violation absent explicit premature-exit evidence; omitted. (6) Initial entry contracts (NL1-INITENTRY-1 root->DoorsClosing, NL5-INITENTRY-1 InMotion->Accelerating) are both satisfied by exact owner-local edges (transition:line:32, transition:line:14) reaching the correct target; omitted per owner-entry satisfaction rule. The single genuine behavioral-consequence issue is the Stopping dead-end frontier fact, captured as a derived V1 deadlock candidate under NL2's InMotion->Stopping obligation scope, since NL2 establishes Stopping as a required continuation state whose complete lack of outgoing transition leaves the system permanently stuck with no further behavior, which is a stronger consequence than the endpoint-existence contract itself decides.
